enhanced_information: In the context of treating aggressive B-cell lymphomas, the most appropriate treatment options should be based on established protocols. Cytoreductive surgery can reduce tumor burden, which may improve the efficacy of subsequent chemotherapy, but it is not typically the first-line treatment for lymphomas. Rituximab-CHOP is a standard regimen for aggressive B-cell lymphomas, with 6-8 cycles recommended for optimal response. Combining Rituximab-CHOP with retroperitoneal radiotherapy can enhance local control and improve survival rates, making it a viable option. Intensive chemotherapy with Rituximab and CNS prophylaxis is crucial for patients at high risk of CNS involvement, addressing both systemic and CNS disease. Delaying treatment until PET-CT may lead to disease progression, which is generally not advisable. Therefore, the most consensus-aligned treatment would be Rituximab-CHOP followed by retroperitoneal radiotherapy, as it combines effective chemotherapy with local control measures.
